sections.name: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself
lines: Your brain is always predicting what your own movements will feel like.
Before you move, a part at the back of your brain, the cerebellum, makes a copy of the plan.
So when your own fingers touch you, your brain already knows, and turns the feeling down.
Someone else's touch is a surprise. And surprises get the full feeling.
In one experiment, a robot added a tiny delay to people's own tickles.
And suddenly, their own touch felt more ticklish.
